title: Complex numbers: powers of i, conjugate, modulus

items: i² = −1, i³ = −i, i⁴ = 1. For iⁿ divide n by 4 and keep the remainder: i⁴³ = i³ = −i.
z = a + bi: conjugate z̄ = a − bi, modulus |z| = √(a² + b²), z·z̄ = |z|².
|z₁z₂| = |z₁||z₂|, |z₁/z₂| = |z₁|/|z₂|, |z₁ + z₂| ≤ |z₁| + |z₂|.
a + bi = c + di ⇔ a = c and b = d.

blocks.text: Real numbers: terminating or recurring decimals are rational; √2, π are irrational. Multiplying an inequality by a negative reverses it.
√(−4)·√(−9) = 2i·3i = −6, not √36. √a·√b = √(ab) fails when both are negative.

items: z = a + bi is the point (a, b): real part on x-axis, imaginary on y-axis.
Polar form: z = r(cos θ + i sin θ), r = |z|, θ = arg z from the positive x-axis.
a = r cos θ, b = r sin θ, tan θ = b/a.
Multiply: moduli multiply, arguments add. Divide: moduli divide, arguments subtract.
|z₁ + z₂| = |z₁| + |z₂| only when z₁, z₂ have equal arguments.

blocks.text: Example: z = −1 + i has r = √2 and lies in quadrant II, so θ = 3π/4 (135°).
tan⁻¹(b/a) alone gives −π/4 for −1 + i. Always place the point first and pick the angle in its quadrant.

title: Square roots of a + bi and conjugate roots

blocks.text: Put √(a + bi) = x + iy and square: x² − y² = a and 2xy = b. Also x² + y² = |a + bi|.

items: Signs: x and y have the same sign if b > 0, opposite signs if b < 0.

blocks.text: Conjugate roots: with real coefficients, if 2 + i is a root so is 2 − i. Quadratic: x² − (sum)x + (product) = x² − 4x + 5.
In an MCQ just square the options: (2 + i)² = 3 + 4i.

title: Sets and logic: counts, De Morgan, negation

items: n(A ∪ B) = n(A) + n(B) − n(A ∩ B).
A set with n elements has 2ⁿ subsets and 2ⁿ − 1 proper subsets: {a, b, c} has 8.
De Morgan: (A ∪ B)′ = A′ ∩ B′, (A ∩ B)′ = A′ ∪ B′; in logic ~(p ∧ q) = ~p ∨ ~q.
p → q is false only when p is true and q is false.
p → q ≡ ~q → ~p (contrapositive). Converse q → p and inverse ~p → ~q are not equivalent.
Negating swaps ∀ and ∃ and negates the inside: ~(∃x, x² − 2x + 3 < 0) is ∀x, x² − 2x + 3 ≥ 0.

blocks.text: The negation of < is ≥, not >.

title: Counting functions; binary operations and groups

blocks.text: Inverse relation R⁻¹ swaps each pair, so domain of R⁻¹ = range of R.
Group: closure, associative, identity, inverse for every element. Abelian if also commutative.

items: (Z, +) and (Q − {0}, ×) are groups.
(Z, ×) is not: only ±1 have inverses.
a * b = a − b on Z is closed but neither commutative nor associative.

blocks.text: In a group the identity is unique and each element has exactly one inverse.

title: Domain, range and types of function

items: One-one: different x give different y (any horizontal line cuts the graph at most once).
Onto: range = co-domain. Bijective: one-one and onto.
Even: f(−x) = f(x), symmetric about the y-axis. Odd: f(−x) = −f(x), symmetric about the origin.
Algebraic (polynomial, rational, roots) vs transcendental (trig, exponential, log).
Ranges to know: x² ≥ 0, eˣ > 0, √x ≥ 0.

blocks.text: f(x) = x² on R is not one-one (f(2) = f(−2)); on x ≥ 0 it is.

items: (f∘g)(x) = f(g(x)): apply g first. In general f∘g ≠ g∘f.
Inverse: write y = f(x), swap x and y, solve for y. f(x) = 2x + 3 gives f⁻¹(x) = (x − 3)/2.
f(x) = (ax + b)/(cx + d) gives f⁻¹(x) = (b − dx)/(cx − a).
Domain of f⁻¹ = range of f; range of f⁻¹ = domain of f.
f(f⁻¹(x)) = x. The graph of f⁻¹ is the mirror image of f in the line y = x.
Only a one-one (bijective) function has an inverse function.

blocks.text: Example: f(x) = √(x − 2), x ≥ 2, has range y ≥ 0, so f⁻¹(x) = x² + 2 with x ≥ 0.
f⁻¹(x) is not 1/f(x).

title: Graph transformations and the parabola vertex

blocks.text: Vertex of y = ax² + bx + c is at x = −b/(2a). y = 2x² − 8x + 3: x = 2, y = −5, vertex (2, −5).
Minus inside the bracket moves the graph right, not left.

items: log(mn) = log m + log n; log(m/n) = log m − log n; log mⁿ = n log m.
Change of base: logₐb = log b / log a, so logₐb · log_b a = 1.
Base as a power: log of b to base aᵏ = (1/k) logₐb, e.g. log₉x = ½ log₃x.
logₐ1 = 0, logₐa = 1, a^(logₐx) = x.
y = aˣ and y = logₐx are inverses (mirror in y = x).

blocks.text: Example: log₃x + log₉x = 3 → (3/2)log₃x = 3 → log₃x = 2 → x = 9.
log(m + n) ≠ log m + log n. After solving, reject any x that makes a log argument ≤ 0.
Examples: (1 − cos 4x)/x² → 16/2 = 8; (5ˣ − 3ˣ)/x → ln 5 − ln 3 = ln(5/3); (1 + a/n)ⁿ → eᵃ.
If θ is in degrees, (sin θ)/θ → π/180, not 1.

items: Rational, x → ∞: compare highest powers. Top lower → 0; equal → ratio of leading coefficients; top higher → ±∞ (sign from the leading terms, so no finite limit).
0/0: factorise or rationalise, cancel (x − a), then substitute.

blocks.text: Continuous at x = a when f(a) exists, left limit = right limit, and both equal f(a).
Example: f = kx + 1 (x ≤ 2), x² − 1 (x > 2). Match at 2: 2k + 1 = 3, so k = 1.

items: (m × n)(n × p) = m × p; the inner sizes must match. Usually AB ≠ BA.
(AB)ᵗ = BᵗAᵗ and (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹A⁻¹ (order reverses).

head: Name
Condition
rows: A² = A, then (I − A)² = I − A

blocks.text: Rotation matrix [[cos θ, −sin θ], [sin θ, cos θ]] squared is the same matrix with 2θ.

items: Swap two rows (or columns): sign changes.
Two equal or proportional rows: determinant 0.
One row multiplied by k: determinant × k.
Add k × one row to another row: no change.
Triangular or diagonal matrix: product of the diagonal.
n × n matrix: |kA| = kⁿ|A| and |adj A| = |A|ⁿ⁻¹.

blocks.text: Example: 3 × 3 with |A| = 4 gives |2A| = 8 × 4 = 32 and |adj A| = 4² = 16.
|kA| is not k|A|: k multiplies every row, so it comes out n times.

items: In general A⁻¹ = adj A / |A|, only if |A| ≠ 0.
AX = B gives X = A⁻¹B.
Cramer's rule: x = Dₓ/D, y = Dᵧ/D, z = D_z/D, where Dₓ has the x-column replaced by the constants.
Rank = number of non-zero rows in echelon form.

blocks.text: Consistent exactly when rank A = rank of the augmented matrix [A | B].
ax² + bx + c = 0: α + β = −b/a, αβ = c/a. New equation: x² − (sum)x + (product) = 0.

head: b² − 4ac
Roots
rows: real, unequal, rational (a, b, c rational)

items: α² + β² = (α + β)² − 2αβ; (α − β)² = (α + β)² − 4αβ.
α³ + β³ = (α + β)³ − 3αβ(α + β).
Roots kα, kβ: replace x by x/k. Roots 1/α, 1/β: swap a and c.

blocks.text: Example: roots of x² − 3x + 5 = 0 doubled: x² − 6x + 20 = 0.

title: Cube and fourth roots of unity

items: Cube roots of 1: 1, ω, ω², with ω = (−1 + i√3)/2 and ω² = (−1 − i√3)/2.
ω³ = 1 and 1 + ω + ω² = 0, so 1 + ω = −ω² and 1 + ω² = −ω.
ω̄ = ω² and 1/ω = ω². Product of the three roots = 1.
ωⁿ: divide n by 3 and keep the remainder. ω²⁹ = ω² (29 = 27 + 2).
Cube roots of 8: 2, 2ω, 2ω².
Fourth roots of 1: 1, −1, i, −i. Sum 0, product −1.

blocks.text: Reduce powers of ω, then use 1 + ω + ω² = 0: (1 + ω − ω²)(1 − ω + ω²) = (−2ω²)(−2ω) = 4.

title: Remainder theorem and quick factor checks

items: Remainder of p(x) ÷ (x − a) is p(a); for (ax − b) it is p(b/a).
(x − a) is a factor exactly when p(a) = 0.
Sum of all coefficients = 0 → (x − 1) is a factor.
Sum of even-power coefficients = sum of odd-power coefficients → (x + 1) is a factor.
Cubic ax³ + bx² + cx + d: sum of roots −b/a, product of roots −d/a.

blocks.text: In synthetic division write 0 for every missing power, e.g. x³ − 7x + 6 → 1, 0, −7, 6.

title: Max/min of a quadratic and quadratic inequalities

items: y = ax² + bx + c turns at x = −b/(2a): minimum if a > 0, maximum if a < 0.
Make the x² coefficient positive. Roots α < β: (x − α)(x − β) < 0 → α < x < β; > 0 → x < α or x > β.

blocks.text: Line meets curve: substitute; D = 0 means it touches. y = x + k touches y = x² − 3x + 5 when x² − 4x + 5 − k has D = 0: k = 1.
Don't multiply by (x − 1) of unknown sign. x/(x − 1) < 2 → (x − 2)/(x − 1) > 0 → x < 1 or x > 2.
Improper fraction (degree of top ≥ degree of bottom): divide first. (x³ + x + 1)/(x² + 1) = x + 1/(x² + 1).
For a non-repeated linear factor (x − a): cover it up and put x = a in what is left. That value is its constant.

items: For (x − a)² the cover-up gives only the constant over (x − a)²; find the other by comparing coefficients.
Treat x² as one letter: 1/(x⁴ − 1) = ½[1/(x² − 1) − 1/(x² + 1)].

blocks.text: Check an answer by putting a simple value such as x = 0 into both sides.

items: nth term: aₙ = a₁ + (n − 1)d.
Arithmetic mean of a and b: A = (a + b)/2.
aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁.
Terms equally far from the middle add the same: a₃ + a₇ = 2a₅ = a₁ + a₉.

blocks.text: Example: a₃ = 7, a₇ = 19 → 4d = 12, d = 3, a₁ = 1, a₁₀ = 28.
Three numbers in A.P.: take a − d, a, a + d. Sum 15 → a = 5; product 80 → 25 − d² = 16, d = ±3, numbers 2, 5, 8.

items: nth term: aₙ = a₁rⁿ⁻¹.
Infinite sum: S∞ = a₁/(1 − r), only when |r| < 1.
Geometric mean G of a and b: G² = ab (G = √(ab) for positive a, b).
Terms equally far from the middle multiply the same: a₂·a₈ = a₅² = a₁·a₉.

blocks.text: Three numbers in G.P.: take a/r, a, ar; their product is a³.
No S∞ for r = 1 or |r| ≥ 1: the series diverges.

title: H.P., A ≥ G ≥ H, and the special sums

items: H.P.: reciprocals form an A.P.; work in reciprocals, then flip back.
Harmonic mean of a and b: H = 2ab/(a + b).
For positive a ≠ b: A > G > H, and G² = AH.
(aⁿ⁺¹ + bⁿ⁺¹)/(aⁿ + bⁿ) is A for n = 0, G for n = −½, H for n = −1.
(a + b)(1/a + 1/b) ≥ 4 for positive a, b (equal when a = b).

blocks.text: There is no simple formula for the sum of an H.P.

items: Counting: tasks done one after another multiply (3 starters, 5 mains → 15 meals); either-or choices add.
Repetition allowed: r places from n things → nʳ.
n things with p alike, q alike: n!/(p! q!). LEVEL → 5!/(2! 2!) = 30.
n things round a circle: (n − 1)!
Necklace or garland (can be turned over): (n − 1)!/2.

blocks.text: "At least one" = total − none. Three-digit numbers with at least one 7: 900 − 8·9·9 = 252.
A number cannot start with 0: the first digit has one choice fewer.

items: ⁿCᵣ = n!/(r!(n − r)!); ⁿPᵣ = r!·ⁿCᵣ.
ⁿCᵣ = ⁿCₙ₋ᵣ; ⁿC₀ = ⁿCₙ = 1.
ⁿCᵣ + ⁿCᵣ₋₁ = ⁿ⁺¹Cᵣ.
ⁿCₓ = ⁿCᵧ means x = y or x + y = n.
From n points, no three in a line: ⁿC₂ lines, ⁿC₃ triangles.
Diagonals of an n-sided polygon: n(n − 3)/2 (octagon: 20).

blocks.text: Order matters (arrange, rank, digits) → permutation. Order does not matter (choose, team, committee) → combination.

items: P(A) = n(A)/n(S), and 0 ≤ P(A) ≤ 1.
P(not A) = 1 − P(A).
P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B).
Mutually exclusive: P(A ∩ B) = 0, so P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B).
Independent: P(A ∩ B) = P(A)·P(B).
n coins: 2ⁿ outcomes. Two dice: 36 outcomes.

blocks.text: Two dice, ways to get sum s: s − 1 for s ≤ 7, and 13 − s for s ≥ 7. Sum ≥ 10: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 ways, P = 1/6.
Mutually exclusive is not the same as independent: two exclusive events with non-zero probabilities are never independent.

items: Step 1: P(1) is true (or P(n₀), the first value).
Step 2: assuming P(k), prove P(k + 1).
Only both steps together prove P(n) for all n.

blocks.text: Right: prove 1 + 2 + … + n = n(n + 1)/2 with both steps.
Wrong: "true for n = 1 to 100, so always true". n² − n + 41 is prime for n = 1 to 40, but at n = 41 it is 41².

items: xⁿ − yⁿ is divisible by x − y for every n.
xⁿ + yⁿ is divisible by x + y when n is odd; xⁿ − yⁿ by x + y when n is even.
n(n + 1)(n + 2) and n³ − n are divisible by 6.
(a + b)ⁿ = Σ ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ, r = 0 to n: n + 1 terms.
General term: Tᵣ₊₁ = ⁿCᵣ aⁿ⁻ʳ bʳ.
Middle term: n even → T(n/2 + 1); n odd → two middle terms T((n + 1)/2) and T((n + 3)/2).
Sum of coefficients = 2ⁿ (put a = b = 1). Odd-placed and even-placed coefficients each add to 2ⁿ⁻¹.
Term free of x: set the power of x in Tᵣ₊₁ equal to 0.

blocks.text: Example: x² coefficient of (1 + kx)⁶ is ⁶C₂k² = 15k² = 60, so k² = 4 and k = ±2 (k = 2 if k > 0).
The rth term uses ⁿCᵣ₋₁, not ⁿCᵣ. Keep the sign of b: in (a − b)ⁿ the terms alternate.
(1 + x)ⁿ = 1 + nx + n(n − 1)x²/2! + n(n − 1)(n − 2)x³/3! + … For n negative or a fraction the series never ends and needs |x| < 1.
Take the constant out first: (a + x)ⁿ = aⁿ(1 + x/a)ⁿ, valid for |x| < |a|.

title: Radians, arc length and standard values

items: π rad = 180°, so 1° = π/180 rad and 1 rad ≈ 57.3°.
Arc length l = rθ, sector area = ½r²θ (θ in radians).

blocks.text: sin of 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90° is √0/2, √1/2, √2/2, √3/2, √4/2; cos runs the same list backwards.
l = rθ needs θ in radians, not degrees.

title: Quadrant signs, points and basic identities

blocks.text: All Students Take Coffee
items: All: quadrant I, all ratios positive
Students: quadrant II, sin and cosec positive
Take: quadrant III, tan and cot positive
Coffee: quadrant IV, cos and sec positive
Point (x, y) on the terminal side: r = √(x² + y²), sin = y/r, cos = x/r, tan = y/x.
sin²θ + cos²θ = 1; 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ; 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.
Given tan α only: divide top and bottom by cos α. tan α = 2 → (sin + cos)/(sin − cos) = 3/1 = 3.

blocks.text: r is always positive. For P(4a, −3a) with a < 0, r = −5a, so sin α = −3a/(−5a) = 3/5.

items: sin(α ± β) = sin α cos β ± cos α sin β.
cos(α ± β) = cos α cos β ∓ sin α sin β (sign flips).
tan(α ± β) = (tan α ± tan β)/(1 ∓ tan α tan β).
Fundamental law: cos(α − β) = cos α cos β + sin α sin β.

blocks.text: Allied angles: 90° ± θ, 270° ± θ swap sin ↔ cos, tan ↔ cot; 180° ± θ, 360° − θ keep the ratio. Sign from the quadrant.
Spot it: cos 80° cos 20° + sin 80° sin 20° = cos 60° = 1/2.

items: sin 2θ = 2 sin θ cos θ = 2 tan θ/(1 + tan²θ).
cos 2θ = cos²θ − sin²θ = 2cos²θ − 1 = 1 − 2sin²θ.
tan 2θ = 2 tan θ/(1 − tan²θ).
sin²(θ/2) = (1 − cos θ)/2; cos²(θ/2) = (1 + cos θ)/2.
tan(θ/2) = (1 − cos θ)/sin θ = sin θ/(1 + cos θ).
sin 3θ = 3 sin θ − 4 sin³θ; cos 3θ = 4 cos³θ − 3 cos θ.
tan 3θ = (3 tan θ − tan³θ)/(1 − 3 tan²θ).

blocks.text: Fix the sign of cos first. sin α = 3/5 in quadrant II: cos α = −4/5, so sin 2α = −24/25.

items: 2 sin A cos B = sin(A + B) + sin(A − B)
2 cos A cos B = cos(A + B) + cos(A − B)
2 sin A sin B = cos(A − B) − cos(A + B)

blocks.text: cos C − cos D carries a minus sign.

title: Domain, range and period of the six functions

blocks.text: Even: cos, sec. Odd: sin, tan, cot, cosec.

items: sin(ax + b), cos(ax + b): period 2π/|a|. tan(ax + b): π/|a|.
sin²x, |sin x|: period π. |sin x| + |cos x|: π/2.
Asymptotes of tan 2x: 2x = π/2 + nπ, so x = π/4, 3π/4 in (0, π).

title: Amplitude, phase shift and max/min values

blocks.text: y = A sin(Bx + C) + D: amplitude |A|, period 2π/|B|, range [D − |A|, D + |A|], phase shift C/B to the left (if C/B > 0).

items: a sin x + b cos x lies between −√(a² + b²) and √(a² + b²): 3 sin x + 4 cos x has max 5.
Restricted x: find the angle's range first. x in [0, π/2] → 2x − π/6 in [−π/6, 5π/6] → 2 sin(2x − π/6) in [−1, 2].
Quadratic in s = sin x: cos 2x + 2 sin x = 1 − 2s² + 2s, max 3/2 at s = 1/2.

blocks.text: sin(2x + π/3) = sin 2(x + π/6): it is sin 2x shifted π/6 left, not π/3.

title: Laws of sines, cosines and tangents

blocks.text: Side a is opposite angle A, b opposite B, c opposite C; R = circumradius.

items: Sines: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C = 2R
Cosines: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A, so cos A = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc)
Tangents: (a − b)/(a + b) = tan((A − B)/2) / tan((A + B)/2)

blocks.text: Heights and distances: angle of elevation from A = angle of depression from B (alternate angles). Draw the right triangle first.
a² > b² + c² means A is obtuse. The largest side faces the largest angle.

title: Area of a triangle and half-angle formulas

blocks.text: s = (a + b + c)/2 is the semi-perimeter; Δ = area.

items: Δ = ½ab sin C = ½bc sin A = ½ca sin B
Hero's formula: Δ = √(s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c))
Δ = a² sin B sin C / (2 sin A)  (one side, all angles)

blocks.text: Check on the 3-4-5 triangle: s = 6, Δ = √(6·3·2·1) = 6 = ½·3·4.
In ½ab sin C the angle must be the one between sides a and b.

items: r r₁ r₂ r₃ = Δ²

blocks.text: Right triangle: R = hypotenuse/2. Equilateral side a: R = a/√3, r = a/(2√3), so R = 2r.
r₁ uses s − a, not s + a: every escribed radius is larger than r.

title: Inverse trig: domains and principal values

items: sin⁻¹(−x) = −sin⁻¹x and tan⁻¹(−x) = −tan⁻¹x
cos⁻¹(−x) = π − cos⁻¹x, e.g. cos⁻¹(−½) = 2π/3

blocks.text: sin⁻¹(sin θ) = θ only when θ is in [−π/2, π/2]. So sin⁻¹(sin 5π/6) = π/6, not 5π/6.

title: Inverse trig sum and difference formulas

items: sin⁻¹x + cos⁻¹x = π/2  (−1 ≤ x ≤ 1)
tan⁻¹x + cot⁻¹x = π/2
tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x + y)/(1 − xy))  if xy < 1
tan⁻¹x − tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹((x − y)/(1 + xy))  if xy > −1
2 tan⁻¹x = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²))  if |x| < 1
sin⁻¹x + sin⁻¹y = sin⁻¹(x√(1 − y²) + y√(1 − x²))  for x, y ≥ 0, x² + y² ≤ 1
cos⁻¹x + cos⁻¹y = cos⁻¹(xy − √(1 − x²)√(1 − y²))  for x + y ≥ 0

blocks.text: If x, y > 0 and xy > 1, add π: tan⁻¹2 + tan⁻¹3 = π + tan⁻¹(−1) = 3π/4, not −π/4.

title: General solutions of sin, cos and tan equations

blocks.text: n is any integer; α is the principal value.
Some books write sin θ = k as θ = nπ + (−1)ⁿα; it is the same set.
tan repeats every π, sin and cos every 2π.

items: Quadratic form: 2sin²θ − sin θ − 1 = 0 → (2sin θ + 1)(sin θ − 1) = 0 → sin θ = 1 or −½.
Reject sin θ or cos θ values outside [−1, 1].
Mixed functions: change to one function with sin² + cos² = 1 or 1 + tan² = sec².
a sin θ + b cos θ = c: write √(a² + b²) sin(θ + φ) = c; solutions exist only if |c| ≤ √(a² + b²).

blocks.text: sin kx = 0 has 2k + 1 zeros on the closed interval [0, 2π] (both ends count): sin 2x has 5.
Never divide by sin θ or cos θ (roots are lost); factor it out. If you squared both sides, test every answer in the original.

title: Derivative definition and the main rules

items: First principles: f′(x) = lim (h → 0) [f(x + h) − f(x)]/h = slope of the tangent
Product: (uv)′ = u′v + uv′
Quotient: (u/v)′ = (vu′ − uv′)/v²
Chain: dy/dx = (dy/du)(du/dx)
Parametric: dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt)
Implicit: differentiate both sides, then collect the dy/dx terms
Logarithmic: y = xˣ → ln y = x ln x → y′ = xˣ(1 + ln x)

blocks.text: Parametric second derivative: d²y/dx² = [d/dt(dy/dx)] ÷ (dx/dt), not (d²y/dt²)/(d²x/dt²).
Quotient rule order: bottom × d(top) first, then minus.
tanh x → sech²x; sinh⁻¹x → 1/√(1 + x²); cosh⁻¹x → 1/√(x² − 1); tanh⁻¹x → 1/(1 − x²).
Every "co" trig function (cos, cot, csc and their inverses) gets a minus sign; cosh does not.

items: Maclaurin: f(x) = f(0) + f′(0)x + f″(0)x²/2! + f‴(0)x³/3! + …
Taylor: f(a + h) = f(a) + h f′(a) + h² f″(a)/2! + …

blocks.text: Coefficient of xⁿ = f⁽ⁿ⁾(0)/n!. sin x is odd, so only odd powers; cos x is even, only even powers.
ln(1 + x) has no factorials, and its signs alternate starting with +x.

items: Tangent at (x₁, y₁): y − y₁ = m(x − x₁), m = f′(x₁); normal slope = −1/m
f′(x) > 0: increasing; f′(x) < 0: decreasing
Critical point: f′(c) = 0 (or f′ undefined)
Second-derivative test: f″(c) < 0 → maximum; f″(c) > 0 → minimum; f″(c) = 0 → test fails
Differential: dy = f′(x) dx, so f(x + δx) ≈ f(x) + f′(x)δx
